sections.h2: Where is Ogden, Utah, and what is its layout?
sections.html:
Ogden is the county seat of Weber County, about 40 miles north of Salt Lake City and 10 miles east of the Great Salt Lake. The city covers 27.55 square miles and sits at about 4,341 feet, rising from the valley floor to the Wasatch foothills on its east side.

The city divides into six districts. The North End includes West Ogden, Downtown and East Central, and the East side includes the East Bench and Shadow Valley. Neighbors include South Ogden, Roy, West Haven, Marriott-Slaterville, Farr West, Harrisville, Pleasant View and North Ogden.

sections.h2: How did Ogden start, and why is it called Junction City?
sections.html:
Ogden began as Fort Buenaventura, founded in 1846 by the trapper Miles Goodyear about a mile west of today's downtown, and it is generally described as the first permanent settlement of European descent in what is now Utah. In November 1847 Captain James Brown bought the fort, the land and livestock for $3,000, and the settlement was called Brownsville.

The city was incorporated on February 6, 1851 and later renamed for the Hudson's Bay Company brigade leader Peter Skene Ogden. Ogden is the closest sizable city to Promontory Summit, where the first transcontinental railroad was joined in 1869, and it became a major rail hub that still handles heavy freight. The local chamber of commerce once adopted the motto, "You can't get anywhere without coming to Ogden." The National Park Service named Ogden a World War II Heritage City on September 17, 2024.

Passenger rail has changed since then. Amtrak ended the Pioneer in 1997, and rail riders now use FrontRunner to reach Salt Lake City and Provo.

The Internal Revenue Service's regional facility is Ogden's largest employer, with more than 5,000 workers. Other large employers include McKay-Dee Hospital, Weber State University, Ogden City School District, Autoliv and Fresenius.

  • Business Depot Ogden is a business park of more than 1,000 acres on part of the former Defense Depot Ogden, which ran from 1941 to 1997 on 1,128 acres. Tenants include Autoliv North America, ENVE Composites and Goode Ski Technologies.
  • Weber State University's Ogden campus covers more than 500 acres with 63 buildings. Fall 2023 enrollment was about 30,536, including concurrent enrollment students.
  • Hill Air Force Base lies just south of Ogden, in Davis County. It was described as the sixth-largest employer in Utah as of 2018 and houses the Ogden Air Logistics Complex and the 388th Fighter Wing's F-35A jets.

The Census Bureau puts average travel time to work in Ogden at 22.5 minutes.

sections.h2: What does Ogden's weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Ogden has hot, fairly dry summers and snowy winters, so a house needs a roof and heating system that cope with both. Summer highs frequently reach 95 degrees, with a record of 106 and a record low of minus 23.

Average annual precipitation is 16.36 inches, with spring the wettest season. Monsoon thunderstorms usually fall between late July and mid-September, and snow generally begins in late October or early November and ends around April.

Ogden also lies along the Wasatch Fault. The Weber segment last produced a major earthquake roughly 200 to 700 years ago, according to Wikipedia's fault entry, and each active segment can produce a quake as large as about magnitude 7.5. A structural check is worth considering for an older house before listing.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and housing types does Ogden have?
sections.html:
Ogden's historic districts include Historic 25th Street, Eccles Avenue and Jefferson Avenue, and other landmarks include Union Station, Peery's Egyptian Theatre and the Ogden Nature Center.

The city's housing element, amended in 2022, says over 44 percent of Ogden's housing was built before 1940, compared with 27.2 percent in Weber County. That figure comes from the plan's older existing conditions section, so treat it as a rough guide.

The same document lists three projects the city approved as moderate-income housing actions: Lotus Riverwalk Phase 2 with 174 units, Meadowbrook with 48 and Capital Square with 176. It also describes the R-9 zone in the 9 Rails Creative District, which allows up to 29 units per acre, and cottage lots of 1,500 square feet within two blocks of the bus rapid transit route.

sections.h2: How do Ogden's schools and addresses work?
sections.html:
Ogden City School District's boundary matches the city limits, and Weber School District serves areas outside the city even when those homes have an Ogden mailing address. A listing that says "Ogden" does not tell a buyer which district the house is in.

Ogden City School District runs Ogden High School and Ben Lomond High School, three junior highs (Highland, Mound Fort and Mount Ogden) and 13 elementary schools, according to Wikipedia. DaVinci Academy of Science and the Arts is a charter school, and Saint Joseph Catholic High School is a private option.

sections.h2: How do trains, buses and the airport serve Ogden?
sections.html:
FrontRunner commuter rail connects Ogden Central Station directly to Salt Lake City. The OGX bus line runs between Ogden Central Station and Weber State University, and other UTA routes reach Brigham City, Weber County and Davis County.

Ogden-Hinckley Airport is Utah's busiest municipal airport, and Breeze Airways provides its only commercial service, with nonstop flights to Orange County, California. Allegiant and Avelo stopped service in May 2022.

sections.h2: What rental and short-term rental rules apply in Ogden?
sections.html:
Ogden requires a license for every residential rental. The city's rental license page says it is unlawful to occupy a residential rental that is not licensed, and that applications are emailed to businesslicense@ogdencity.com. An invoice follows, and payment is required before the license is issued.

Short-term rentals face tighter limits under city code 15-13-38.

  • A sale voids a short-term rental license unless the new owner gets a new one within 90 days and before operating.
  • In R-1 zones only owner-occupied rentals are allowed, and a non-owner-occupied rental in a residential zone needs three years of continuous ownership.
  • Non-owner-occupied units are inspected every two years, and a revoked property is barred from short-term use for three years.
  • Occupancy is capped at two people per sleeping room, and parking must be on site.

If you are selling a house that has been used as an Airbnb, check your license status before the buyer's agent asks.

sections.h2: How do Weber County property taxes work for an Ogden home?
sections.html:
Weber County bills Ogden property taxes, and the treasurer's page lists the 2026 schedule below. All property is valued as it stood on January 1.

Step2026 and 2027 date
Valuation notices mailedAbout July 20, 2026
Deadline to appeal valuesSeptember 15, 2026 (within 45 days of the notice)
Tax notices mailedOctober 17, 2026
Deadline to pay without penaltyNovember 30, 2026
Delinquent, penalty appliedDecember 1, 2026, the greater of 1% or $10
Interest beginsFebruary 1, 2027, retroactive to January 1

Appeals go to the Clerk/Auditor at 2380 Washington Blvd, Suite 320, and the notice comes with an application. The notice does not show tax relief, which appears on the tax notice.

The Weber County Recorder's fee schedule lists $45 for the first page of a recording and nothing for additional pages, with $2 for each description over ten. Those fees reflect changes effective May 6, 2026.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for an Ogden seller?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Ogden skips the listing, the buyer's loan and the appraisal. You tell us about the house, we make an offer based on its condition, and a title company handles signing and recording.

Ogden sellers often have older houses, rentals or inherited property, and some are still holding a rental license or a short-term rental permit. We can review those details with you before an offer.

faqs.q: What is the population of Ogden, Utah?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau counted 87,321 people in Ogden in 2020. The estimate shown at the top of this page is the more recent figure.

faqs.q: When are Weber County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Weber County lists November 30, 2026 as the deadline to pay without penalty. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, with a penalty of the greater of 1 percent or $10.

faqs.q: Is every Ogden address in Ogden City School District?
faqs.a: No. Ogden City School District matches the city limits, while Weber School District serves areas outside it even if the address says Ogden.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out a house in Ogden?
faqs.a: Yes, Ogden requires a license for all residential rentals, and it is unlawful to occupy an unlicensed rental. Short-term rentals carry additional limits, including a 90-day window for a new owner after a sale.

faqs.q: What is the largest employer in Ogden?
faqs.a: The Internal Revenue Service's regional facility is the largest, with more than 5,000 employees. McKay-Dee Hospital, Weber State University and Autoliv are among the other major employers.
